N-27 SLICE 2 DESIGN, part 1 of 2 (B-131: retire song rows nobody points at; lead, 14 Nov 2026; the advisor's two questions answered from the schema in server/encore_server/encore_server/migrations).

WHAT POINTS AT A SERVER REF (each one is a reason NOT to retire it): song_file.ref (a kept or found file); playlist_entry.ref (any person's playlist); library_item.target where kind='like' (any person; the same table holds saved albums and followed artists whose target is NOT a ref); play_event.ref (a play of any person); import_entry.ref; saved_album_ref.ref (the songs of a saved release); work_item.ref (queued or running background work: keep, prepare, match); playback_state.ref and playback_state.queue (a JSON ARRAY of refs per person: no foreign key, read it as text); ref_merge.into_id (a SURVIVOR that older ids resolve to: never retire the target of a tombstone, clients carry the old ids); file_log.ref (no foreign key: a log of file changes; its rows for a retired ref go with it).

THE N-13 VERDICT lives ON the ref (missing_reason, missing_at, missing_tried_at, missing_rev). A ref with a LIVE verdict (missing.standing_of(row, now).live: 7 days from the last try, same matcher revision) is KEPT for the length of its window, because deleting it forgets the memory that saves YouTube look-ups. After the window an expired verdict is worth nothing and the ref may go.

THE RULE (one sentence): a server ref is retired when NOTHING above points at it, it has no live N-13 verdict, and it is older than 14 days (created_at; and, when it has a verdict, missing_tried_at + the window). The age guard keeps a ref that a tap has just made (resolve, then play within seconds) safe, and a person who searched yesterday and taps today still finds the ref. 'Nobody points at it' means NOBODY AMONG ALL PEOPLE: another person's like, entry or play keeps the ref for everybody. That answers 'what does nobody points at mean for a ref another person may point at'.
